description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Compromised credentials may be used to bypass access controls placed on various resources on systems within the network and may even be used for persistent access to remote systems and externally available services, such as VPNs, Outlook Web Access and remote desktop. In the SentinelMesh lab, this technique is exercised twice: (S3) the authservice database is pre-seeded with a default admin account (admin/admin123) that an attacker can use directly; (S7) the Grafana dashboard is deployed with the default admin password never changed and anonymous read access enabled (GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true), allowing access without any credential at all.

log_tail.pattern: login_attempt event where result=success and identifier=admin (S3 authservice). For S7 Grafana: HTTP POST /login returning status 200, or GET /api/dashboards/home returning status 200 with no authenticated identity.

mitigation: Change all default credentials immediately upon deployment. Disable or remove unused default accounts. Enforce a password change policy for any service that ships with static credentials. Disable anonymous access on all internal dashboards and monitoring tools. Audit authentication logs for logins using known-default usernames.
